In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the efficiency of the alpha particle in producing single-strand breaks in DNA was found to be 72 eV per break and the yield 1.39 per 100 eV.
the DNA damage induced by high energy alpha particles is not significantly different from the damage induced by low energy alpha particles.
alpha particle-induced single-strand breakage of DNA is a linear, single-hit, non-energetic process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DNA is sensitive to high energy alpha particles and the sensitivity is not affected by the state of the film of DNA.
the DNA film technique is a very sensitive and convenient method of studying the effect of ionizing radiation on the DNA.
the efficiency of single-strand break formation by alpha-particles in DNA is 2.5 times greater than that by X-rays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA film technique can be used to study radiation-induced damage to DNA in the absence of oxygen.
the DNA damage induced by alpha particles in the form of single strand breaks is a function of dose.
a dry thin film of DNA is a suitable material for the study of radiation damage to DNA by high energy heavy ions.
